precepts.text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. So the glass is talking about the Bible. We do not understand everything in here. And even when I say that, there are different levels. There are double meanings to many scriptures. But when the Lord returns, then shall we know. What does that last part mean? He created us from the beginning. Before the earth was made, he created us.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.” The glass is talking about the Bible. We do not understand everything in it. Even in saying that, there are different levels, and there are double meanings to many scriptures.

“now I know in part”: we know partially. “but then shall I know”: when the Lord returns, then shall we know. That is the face to face of Ezekiel 20:35, when he pleads with us face to face, and it is how “all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.”

“even as also I am known.” What does that part mean? He created us from the beginning. Before the earth was made, he created us. He already knows us fully; when he returns we will know as we are known, and the children of Israel will be taught of the Lord himself.

precepts.text: For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. That is the glass. note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

precepts.text: Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them. That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures.
precepts.point: For now we see through a glass, darkly. So what is the glass referring to?

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

precepts.text: Paul speaks of understanding all mysteries.
precepts.point: The natural man cannot receive or know the things of the Spirit.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”. Paul was one who understood that mystery. He wrote: “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains”.

Prophecy is a gift, and Paul had the gift of prophecy. He understood all mysteries. That is why, when we read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul explained a lot of things and took them to another level, making them plain for us, even things in the law that we do not fully understand.

He had all knowledge and all faith. So when Paul says “we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery”, he is speaking as a man who was given to understand the mysteries, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the world unto our glory. That hidden wisdom goes into Christ: who he was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages, and even the princes of this world did not know it, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

precepts.text: Charity never faileth, but prophecies shall fail, tongues shall cease, and knowledge shall vanish away.
precepts.point: In the last days the pattern is to call the elders of the church to pray over the sick and anoint with oil, for prophecies, tongues, and such knowledge would cease once the name of Christ was established.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away.”

These gifts of healing and tongues were for that time, to introduce the Son of God and prove the power of the Most High on earth. Once the name of Christ was established, prophecies, tongues and such knowledge would cease. They are not the gifts of today, which is why our people still die of disease no matter what the pastors claim.

We see through this Bible darkly; we don't see everything yet. “but then face to face: now I know in part;” Now we know in part. “but then shall I know even as also I am known.” Exactly. A lot of times people say, "What's going to happen after the thousand-year reign? What's going to happen when the kingdom comes down?" It doesn't say. We got to wait till the Lord comes and ask him. He'll tell us. That's what Paul's talking about.

points: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.

Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth. Charity does not rejoice in sin. If you have the spirit of charity, you are going to suffer long. You are going to be kind. You are not going to envy. You are not going to vaunt yourself. We just read that in Matthew: we are meant to be ministers to the people, not to be ministered to. And it rejoices in the truth. We rejoice in the application of God's laws. We love when we come into a school and we see the school is in order, the men are in order, the men know the scriptures. You sit down and ask some questions. You have been around for nine years and you cannot break down John 3:16 or Galatians 3? We look to the leaders there and say, okay, you are not doing your job. You are not preparing these men.

So the people gather in, but then you do not have charity. Give me the adjectives that you do not have. The lack of charity is that you lack meekness, you are not longsuffering, you are not kind, you do not suffer long. Those things will run the people away. The people will leave. That is why Paul said, restore such a one in a spirit of meekness, lest thou also be tempted. So you can teach all these scriptures, know all these breakdowns, have a photographic memory, but if you do not know how to deal right with the people, the people will not stay.

points: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face. We see through this veil: Christ's body was a veil, letting you know the flesh is a veil; this body is a tabernacle, and we groan in it, waiting for the redemption of our bodies. Once we have our real body, no more obstruction from the groanings of this physical body.

The only way you are going to have clarity in this body is if you feed your spirit every day, in some way, shape, or form: audio classes, a few verses even if the day was intense and you cannot do your four chapters. Four chapters is the standard, but if you cannot do that, still engage with God's word and feed your spirit.

The glass is like a mirror: it is hard to see your true inner man in this flesh, and the only way to have some clarity is to wipe that mirror clean by feeding yourself daily. Know ye not your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? The way you become reprobate begins with not consuming the word every day.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: Hear that: charity thinketh no evil. When Satan comes to put evil thoughts in your mind about someone else, you have to say: I am not going to think evil about that person. Repeat it over and over: charity thinketh no evil. That is how you deal with it when Satan tries to put evil thoughts in your mind. Somebody says something; charity says that person probably did not mean it like that.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: For now we see through a glass, darkly. Why do we see in the glass darkly? Remember what God told Moses: some things I want you to hide. We get bits and pieces; one of the apostles explains it here and there, and we start putting the full picture together, but we are still seeing in parts.

Now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. When Christ returns, he is going to teach us face to face, everything in those other 70 books and everything we are confused about right now. That is why you will never hear us say we have 100 percent truth: the scripture says we know in part. The part we have is these 80 books, and even with them we are missing the other books. The Most High has it that way because our flesh cannot contain some of these things.
